questions.q: Why do companies maintain both a corporate book and a tax book for the same assets?
options: Because corporate books are only used for retired assets
Because financial statement reporting and tax reporting legitimately require different depreciation rules
Because Oracle Fusion Assets requires exactly two books per company
Because tax books replace corporate books after five years
questions.explain: The same real asset can be depreciated differently for financial statements versus tax filing, so a tax book and a corporate book both exist to answer different reporting questions.

questions.q: How does a tax book typically get populated with new asset additions?
options: Through manual data entry identical to the corporate book
Through the mass copy process, which copies additions from the associated corporate book
Tax books cannot contain assets
By importing directly from the General Ledger
questions.explain: Mass copy copies asset additions (and often subsequent transactions) from a corporate book into its associated tax book automatically.

questions.q: When mass copy creates an asset in the tax book, which category book defaults determine its depreciation there?
options: The corporate book's category book defaults
The tax book's own category book defaults
No defaults are applied; depreciation must be entered manually
The defaults from whichever book was created first
questions.explain: The tax book's own category book record determines depreciation method, life, and convention for the copied asset, not the corporate book's.

questions.q: Which of these is expected to stay the same between a corporate book and its associated tax book for a given asset?
options: The depreciation method
The prorate convention
The asset's original cost and date placed in service
Whether bonus depreciation applies
questions.explain: Because both books depreciate the same real-world asset, its underlying cost and date placed in service should stay consistent even though depreciation method and life can differ.

questions.q: Is mass copy a one-time event performed only at implementation?
options: Yes, it only runs once when the tax book is first created
No, it runs periodically to keep the tax book synchronized with ongoing corporate book activity
No, it only runs when an asset is retired
Yes, and any assets added afterward must be entered manually into the tax book
questions.explain: Mass copy runs on an ongoing periodic basis so that additions, adjustments, transfers, and retirements in the corporate book keep propagating into the tax book over time.
